questions.title: Original Population
questions.question: The population of a city is increased by 30% and thus became 78000. What is the original population?

questions.title: Change in Savings
questions.question: A saves 20% of his income. His income is increased by 20% and so he increased his expenditure by 30%. What is the percentage change in his savings? (Enter the magnitude of the change.)
questions.solution: Income 100, savings 20, expenditure 80. New income 120, new expenditure 104, new savings 16. Savings decrease by 4/20 = 20%.

questions.title: Total Votes Polled
questions.question: In an election between two candidates, A and B, A secured 56% of the votes and won by 48000 votes. Find the total number of votes polled if 20% of the votes were declared invalid.
questions.solution: Margin = 56% − 44% = 12% of valid votes = 48000, so valid votes = 400000. Valid = 80% of total, so total = 400000 / 0.8 = 500000.

questions.title: Reduced Price of Sugar
questions.question: A reduction of 10% in the price of sugar enables a housewife to buy 5 kg more for Rs. 300. Find the reduced price per kg of sugar.
questions.solution: Let the original price be p. 300/(0.9p) − 300/p = 5 → (300/p)(1/9) = 5 → p = 300/45 = 20/3. Reduced price = 0.9 × 20/3 = Rs. 6 per kg.

questions.title: Percentage Correction
questions.question: In a list of weights of candidates appearing for police selections, the weight of A is marked as 58 kg instead of 46.4 kg. Find the percentage of correction required.
questions.solution: Correction = 58 − 46.4 = 11.6 kg. Percentage = 11.6 / 58 × 100 = 20% (decrease).

questions.title: Minimum Pass Marks
questions.question: In an examination, a student secures 40% and fails by 10 marks. If he scored 50%, he would pass by 15 marks. Find the minimum marks required to pass the exam.

questions.title: Oil to Fill the Tank
questions.question: If 240 litres of oil is poured into a tank, it is still 20% empty. How much more oil is to be poured to fill the tank? (in litres)
questions.solution: 240 L = 80% of capacity, so capacity = 300 L. More oil needed = 300 − 240 = 60 L.

questions.title: Difference in Hikes
questions.question: A and B were hired for the same salary. A got two 40% hikes whereas B got a 90% hike. What is the percentage difference in the hikes they got?
questions.solution: A's net hike = 1.4 × 1.4 = 1.96, i.e. 96%. B's hike = 90%. Difference = 96% − 90% = 6%.

questions.title: Population Two Years Ago
questions.question: The population of a town increases at a rate of 10% for every year. If the present population is 12100, find the population two years ago.
questions.solution: Population two years ago = 12100 / (1.1)² = 12100 / 1.21 = 10000.

questions.title: Total Votes Polled (Majority)
questions.question: In an election 10% of the votes were invalid. 40% of the votes were for A and the rest to B. B won with a majority of 243 votes. The total number of votes polled is:
questions.solution: Of the valid votes, A gets 40% and B gets 60%, so the majority = 20% of valid = 243 → valid = 1215. Valid = 90% of total, so total = 1215 / 0.9 = 1350.

questions.title: Gain Percentage from Equal Fractions
questions.question: One-fifth of the cost price, one-seventh of the marked price and one-sixth of the selling price are all equal. What is the gain percentage of the trader?
questions.solution: Let CP/5 = MP/7 = SP/6 = k, so CP = 5k, SP = 6k. Gain = k/5k = 20%.

questions.title: Profit % on Toffees
questions.question: A shopkeeper buys toffees at the rate of 40 for Rs. 5 and sells at the rate of 50 for Rs. 10. The profit % is:

questions.title: Actual Profit %
questions.question: A shopkeeper had calculated profit % on SP and announced it as 40%. His actual profit % (on CP) is: (round off to 2 decimals)
questions.solution: Let SP = 100, profit = 40, so CP = 60. Actual profit % = 40/60 × 100 = 66.67%.

questions.title: Cost Price of Radio
questions.question: A radio was sold for 18% profit. If it were sold for Rs. 30 more, a profit of 20% would have been gained. Find the CP.

questions.title: Lemons Bought for a Rupee
questions.question: A vendor sells lemons at 5 for a rupee, gaining 40%. How many did he buy for a rupee?
questions.solution: SP per lemon = 1/5. CP per lemon = (1/5)/1.4 = 1/7. So he bought 7 lemons for a rupee.

questions.title: Gain by Selling at 2040
questions.question: Saleem lost 20% by selling a bicycle for 1536. What percent shall he gain by selling it for 2040?

questions.title: False Meter Scale
questions.question: A cloth merchant says that due to the slump in the market, he sells the cloth at 10% loss. But he uses a false meter scale and gains 20%. How much less does he measure for a meter? (in cm)
questions.solution: Let CP per true metre = 1. He sells x metres of cloth (cost x) for 0.9. Gain: (0.9 − x)/x = 0.2 → x = 0.75 m. So he measures 25 cm less.

questions.title: Loss % of Fruit Vendor
questions.question: A fruit vendor buys 10 bananas for 14 and sells them at 12 for 15. Find his loss percentage. (round off to 2 decimals)
questions.solution: CP per banana = 1.4, SP per banana = 1.25. Loss % = 0.15/1.4 × 100 = 10.71% (loss).

questions.title: Profit % on Apples
questions.question: 100 apples are bought at 350 and sold at the rate of 48 per dozen. What is the profit % (round off to 2 decimals)?
questions.solution: SP per apple = 48/12 = 4, so SP of 100 apples = 400. Profit % = 50/350 × 100 = 14.29%.

questions.title: Marked Price Percentage
questions.question: How much percent above the cost price should a shopkeeper mark his goods so that after allowing a discount of 25% on the marked price, he gains 20%?
questions.solution: 0.75 × MP = 1.2 CP → MP = 1.6 CP, i.e. 60% above CP.

questions.title: Quantity of Costlier Rice
questions.question: How many kg of rice costing 9 per kg must be mixed with 27 kg of rice costing 7 per kg so that there may be a gain of 10% by selling the mixture at 9.24 per kg? (The source text read 19; 9 is used here as it is the only value that gives a clean answer.)
questions.solution: Cost price of mixture = 9.24 / 1.1 = 8.4. By alligation, (cost 7 qty) : (cost 9 qty) = (9 − 8.4) : (8.4 − 7) = 0.6 : 1.4 = 3 : 7. So 27 kg ↔ 3 parts, and the costlier rice = 27 × 7/3 = 63 kg.

questions.title: Mixing Milk-Water Vessels
questions.question: Two vessels P and Q contain milk and water mixed in the ratio 8:5 and 5:2 respectively. In what ratio should these two mixtures be mixed to get a new mixture containing 69 3/13 % milk? (P : Q)

questions.title: Water to be Added (60 L)
questions.question: In a mixture of 60 litres, the ratio of milk and water is 2:1. What amount of water must be added to make the ratio of milk and water 1:2? (in litres)

questions.title: Ratio of Sugar Varieties
questions.question: Find the ratio in which sugar at 7.20 a kg be mixed with sugar at 5.70 a kg to produce a mixture worth 6.30 a kg. (7.20 : 5.70)

questions.title: Wheat Flour at 18% Profit
questions.question: A merchant has 1000 kg of wheat flour, part of which he sells at 8% profit and the rest at 18% profit. He gains 14% on the whole. Find the quantity (in kg) he sold at 18% profit.

questions.title: Rate of Second Sugar
questions.question: One quality of sugar at 9.30 per kg is mixed with another quality at a certain rate in the ratio 8:7. If the mixture so formed is worth ₹10 per kg, what is the rate per kg of the second quality?

questions.title: Milk Cans Mixed
questions.question: A milk vendor has two cans of milk. The first contains 25% water and the rest milk. The second has 50% water. How much quantity (in litres) should be mixed from each container to get 12 litres of mixture where the ratio of water to milk is 3:5?
questions.solution: Required water fraction = 3/8 = 37.5%. Alligation: (50 − 37.5) : (37.5 − 25) = 1 : 1. So 6 L from each can.

questions.title: Spirit and Water Vessels
questions.question: Two vessels A and B contain spirit and water mixed in the ratio 5:2 and 7:6 respectively. Find the ratio in which these mixtures be mixed to obtain a new mixture in vessel C containing spirit and water in the ratio 8:5. (A : B)

questions.title: Water to be Added (48 L)
questions.question: In a mixture of 48 litres, the ratio of milk and water is 2:1. If this ratio is to be 1:3, what is the quantity of water (in litres) to be further added?

questions.title: Ratio of Rice Varieties
questions.question: In what ratio must a grocer mix two varieties of rice worth 40 per kg and 48 per kg so that by selling the mixture at 50.6 per kg he may gain 10%? (40 : 48)

questions.title: Words from SCARY
questions.question: How many words can be made from the word "SCARY" using all the alphabets with repetition and without repetition respectively?
questions.solution: With repetition: 5^5 = 3125. Without repetition: 5! = 120.

questions.title: 4-digit Numbers Divisible by 5
questions.question: How many 4-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 which are divisible by 5 when none of the digits are repeated?
questions.solution: Last digit must be 5. The other three places: 6 × 5 × 4 = 120.

questions.title: DERAIL Vowels at Odd Positions
questions.question: In how many ways can the alphabets of the word 'DERAIL' be arranged so that the vowels come at the odd positions only and no letters are repeated?
questions.solution: Vowels E, A, I take the 3 odd positions in 3! = 6 ways; consonants D, R, L take the 3 even positions in 3! = 6 ways. Total = 36.

questions.title: Words from UNITED
questions.question: How many words can be made from the letters of the word 'UNITED' taking all the letters at a time considering no letter is to be repeated?
questions.solution: All 6 letters are distinct: 6! = 720.

questions.title: 4-digit Numbers without Repetition
questions.question: How many 4-digit numbers can be formed using the digits (1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9) when repetition of digits is not allowed?

questions.title: New Words from ALIVE
questions.question: Find the number of new words that can be formed by rearranging the letters of the word 'ALIVE'.
questions.solution: Total arrangements = 5! = 120. New words exclude the original word: 120 − 1 = 119.

questions.title: EASYQUIZ Vowels Together
questions.question: What is the number of possible words that can be made using the word "EASYQUIZ" such that the vowels always come together?
questions.solution: Vowels E, A, U, I (4) are treated as one unit, giving 5 units: 5! = 120. Vowels can be arranged among themselves in 4! = 24 ways. Total = 120 × 24 = 2880.

questions.title: Numbers with Distinct Digits
questions.question: How many numbers are there between 100 and 1000 in which all the digits are distinct?
questions.solution: 3-digit numbers: first digit 9 ways (1–9), second 9 ways, third 8 ways: 9 × 9 × 8 = 648.

questions.title: Men to Build a Wall
questions.question: If 72 men can build a wall 280 m long in 21 days, how many men will take 18 days to build a similar wall of length 100 m?

questions.title: B Alone
questions.question: A takes twice as much time as B or thrice as much time as C to finish a piece of work. Working together, they can finish the work in 2 days. B can do the work alone in (days):
questions.solution: Let B take b days, then A takes 2b and C takes 2b/3. 1/(2b) + 1/b + 3/(2b) = 3/b = 1/2 → b = 6 days.

questions.title: Men to Discharge
questions.question: A contractor undertook to finish a certain work in 124 days and employed 120 men on it. After 64 days, he found that he had already done 2/3 of the work. How many men can he discharge now so that the work may finish in time?
questions.solution: 2/3 work in 64 days by 120 men → total work = 120 × 64 × 3/2 = 11520 man-days. Remaining 1/3 = 3840 man-days in 60 days → 64 men. Discharge 120 − 64 = 56.

questions.title: Time for 1/8th Work
questions.question: A can do 3/4 of a work in 12 days. In how many days can he finish 1/8 of the work?
questions.solution: Full work = 12 / (3/4) = 16 days. 1/8 of work = 2 days.

questions.title: Charlie Alone
questions.question: Peter does 75% of work in 12 days. He then calls Charlie for help and they both complete the rest of the work in 3 days. How many days would Charlie have taken to complete the work alone?
questions.solution: Peter's rate = 1/16 per day. In 3 days Peter does 3/16. Remaining 25% = 4/16, so Charlie does 1/16 in 3 days. Charlie alone = 48 days.

questions.title: A and B Together
questions.question: If A is twice as good a workman as B and therefore is able to finish a job in 40 days less than B, how many days will it take to finish the same job if A and B work together? (round off to 2 decimals)

questions.title: C's Share of Money
questions.question: Worker A alone can do a piece of work in 6 days and B alone in 8 days. A and B undertook to do it for ₹4000. With the help of worker C, they completed the work in 3 days. How much money (in ₹) will be given to C?
questions.solution: A + B in 3 days = 3 × (1/6 + 1/8) = 7/8. C does the remaining 1/8, so C's share = 4000/8 = ₹500.

questions.title: A Alone (Efficiency)
questions.question: A and B can do a job together in 7 days. A is 1 3/4 times as efficient as B. How long (in days) does it take for A to do it alone?
questions.solution: Efficiency A : B = 7 : 4. Total work = 11 × 7 = 77 units. A alone = 77 / 7 = 11 days.

questions.title: A's Wages
questions.question: A and B can do a work in 10 and 12 days. They start the work and B leaves after three days. If daily wages are Rs. 20 for each, how much (in Rs.) does A get?
questions.solution: Work in 3 days together = 3 × (1/10 + 1/12) = 11/20. Remaining 9/20 by A = 4.5 days. A works 7.5 days × 20 = Rs. 150.

questions.title: Days with Different Hours
questions.question: 12 men can do a work in 15 days working 8 hours a day. In how many days can 9 men do the same work, working 10 hours a day?

questions.title: Remaining Part Filled by C
questions.question: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 20, 30 and 45 minutes respectively. A is opened for 5 minutes and closed. B is opened for 6 minutes and then closed. In how many minutes will the remaining part be filled by C?
questions.solution: A fills 5/20 = 1/4, B fills 6/30 = 1/5, total 9/20. Remaining 11/20 by C = 11/20 × 45 = 24.75 minutes.

questions.title: Alternate Pipes with Continuous C
questions.question: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 30, 40 and 60 min respectively. A and B work in alternate minutes, A beginning, whereas C works continuously. In how many minutes will the tank be filled?
questions.solution: Every 2 minutes: 1/30 + 1/40 + 2/60 = 11/120. After 20 min = 110/120. 21st min (A + C): 6/120 → remaining 4/120. 22nd min (B + C) rate 5/120 → 4/5 min. Total = 21.8 min.

questions.title: Capacity of the Tank
questions.question: A tank has a leak which would empty it in 8 hrs. A tap is turned on which admits 6 litres of water a minute into the tank, and it is now emptied in 12 hrs. How many litres does the tank hold?

questions.title: Third Pipe Empties
questions.question: Two pipes A and B can separately fill a cistern in 60 and 75 minutes respectively. There is a third pipe at the bottom that empties it. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, the cistern is full in 50 minutes. In how much time (minutes) can the third pipe alone empty the cistern?

questions.title: Two Fill Pipes Together
questions.question: One fill pipe A is 2 times faster than the second fill pipe B. If A can fill a cistern in 9 minutes, find the time (minutes) when the cistern will be full if both fill pipes are opened together.
questions.solution: B takes 18 min. Together: 1/9 + 1/18 = 1/6 → 6 min.

questions.title: Reservoir Filled by P Alone
questions.question: A reservoir is provided with two pipes P and Q. P can fill the reservoir 5 hours faster than Q. If both together fill the reservoir in 6 hours, the reservoir will be filled by P alone in (hours):
questions.solution: Let P take x hours, Q x + 5. 1/x + 1/(x+5) = 1/6 → x² − 7x − 30 = 0 → x = 10.

questions.title: Pipe A Turned Off
questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 15 and 20 minutes respectively. Both pipes are opened together but after 4 minutes, pipe A is turned off. What is the total time required to fill the tank? (round off to 2 decimals)

questions.title: Three Pipes Together
questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 4 hours and 8 hours respectively. Pipe C can empty it in 16 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, how long (hours) will it take to fill the tank?
questions.solution: Net rate = 1/4 + 1/8 − 1/16 = 5/16 per hour → 16/5 = 3.2 hours.

questions.title: When B is Turned Off
questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 37.5 minutes and 45 minutes respectively. Both pipes are opened initially. After how long (minutes) is pipe B turned off, if the cistern is to be filled in half an hour?
questions.solution: A runs the full 30 min: 30/37.5 = 4/5. B must fill 1/5: t/45 = 1/5 → t = 9 min.

questions.title: Capacity with 5 L/min Tap
questions.question: A leak can empty a tank in 8 hours. Another tap is opened which pours 5 litres of water a minute into the tank, and now it is emptied in 12 hours. How many litres does the tank hold?

questions.title: Time Taken by First Person
questions.question: The ratio between rates of walking of two persons is 3:4. If the time taken by the 2nd person to cover a certain distance is 36 minutes, what would be the time (minutes) taken by the first person to cover the same distance?
questions.solution: Time is inversely proportional to speed: t1 : t2 = 4 : 3. t1 = 36 × 4/3 = 48 min.

questions.title: Average Speed
questions.question: A car driver makes his journey at a speed of 75 km/hr and returns to the initial place at 50 km/hr. What is his average speed (km/hr) for the journey?
questions.solution: Average speed = 2 × 75 × 50 / (75 + 50) = 60 km/hr.

questions.title: Original Speed
questions.question: A car travels 715 km at a uniform speed. If the speed of the car is 10 kmph more, it takes 2 hours less to cover the same distance. What was the original speed (kmph)?

questions.title: Distance Between Office and Home
questions.question: Manish goes to office at a speed of 7 km/hr and returns to his home at a speed of 4 km/hr. If he takes 22 hours in total, what is the distance (km) between his office and home?

questions.title: Distance Run by Thief
questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 200 m. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. Assuming the speed of the thief is 10 km/hr and that of the policeman is 12 km/hr, how far (in metres) does the thief run before he is caught?
questions.solution: Relative speed = 2 km/hr. Time = 0.2 / 2 = 0.1 hr. Thief runs 10 × 0.1 = 1 km = 1000 m.

questions.title: Time Walking Both Ways
questions.question: Rahul takes 6 hours in walking to a certain place and riding back. However, he would have gained 2 1/2 hours if he rides both ways. How long (hours) would he take in walking both ways?
questions.solution: Riding both ways = 3.5 h, so riding one way = 1.75 h. Walking one way = 6 − 1.75 = 4.25 h. Walking both ways = 8.5 h.

questions.title: Speed to Catch the Train
questions.question: A man misses a train by 40 minutes if he travels at 30 kmph. If he travels at 40 kmph, he still misses the train by 10 minutes. What is the minimum speed (kmph) required to catch the train on time?

questions.title: Original Duration of Flight
questions.question: In a flight of 600 km, an aircraft was slowed down due to bad weather. Its average speed for the trip was reduced by 200 km/hr and the time of the flight increased by 30 minutes. What is the original duration (hours) of the flight?

questions.title: Distance from House to School
questions.question: Travelling at a speed of 8 kmph a student reaches school from his house 10 minutes early. If he travels at 6 kmph, he is late by 20 minutes. Find the distance (km) between the school and the house.

questions.title: Distance Between Two Towns
questions.question: A bus between two towns reaches its destination 10 minutes early when it moves at 25 km/hr and 15 minutes early when it moves at 30 km/hr. What is the distance (km) between the two towns?

questions.title: Train Crossing Platform
questions.question: If a train 110 m long passes a signal pole in 3 sec, then the time taken (sec) by it to cross a railway platform 165 m long is:

questions.title: Engine Crossing Train
questions.question: An engine of 10 m length travels at 60 kmph. How long (sec) does it take to cross another train 170 m long, running at 54 kmph in the same direction?
questions.solution: Relative speed = 6 kmph = 5/3 m/s. Distance = 180 m. Time = 180 × 3/5 = 108 sec.

questions.title: Trains in Opposite Directions
questions.question: Two trains 220 metres and 380 metres in length are running in opposite directions, one at 35 kmph and the other at 25 kmph. In what time (sec) will they cross each other completely?
questions.solution: Relative speed = 60 kmph = 50/3 m/s. Distance = 600 m. Time = 600 × 3/50 = 36 sec.

questions.title: Still Water and Stream Speed
questions.question: A man can row 30 km downstream in 3 hours 45 minutes, and 11 km upstream in 2 hours 12 minutes. What is the speed of the man in still water and the speed of the stream (in kmph)?
questions.solution: Downstream = 30 / 3.75 = 8 kmph. Upstream = 11 / 2.2 = 5 kmph. Still water = (8 + 5)/2 = 6.5; stream = (8 − 5)/2 = 1.5.

questions.title: More Distance Downstream
questions.question: A man rows 22 km upstream in 4 hours and 45 km downstream in 6 hours. In 10 hours how much more distance (km) can he row downstream than the distance he can row upstream?
questions.solution: Upstream = 5.5 kmph, downstream = 7.5 kmph. In 10 h: 75 km − 55 km = 20 km.

questions.title: Upstream Distance
questions.question: A person can row 10 km in 1 hour in still water. If the speed of the water current is 2 kmph and it takes two hours for him to go to a certain place and back, find the distance (km) he travelled upstream.
questions.solution: Upstream = 8, downstream = 12. d/8 + d/12 = 2 → 5d/24 = 2 → d = 9.6 km.

questions.title: Speed of the Stream
questions.question: A boat can travel 10 kmph in still water. It travelled 91 km downstream and then returned, taking altogether 20 hours. Find the speed of the stream (kmph).

questions.title: B Beats C
questions.question: In a 1 km race, A beats B by 100 m and C by 150 m. In a 2700 m race, by how many metres does B beat C?
questions.solution: When B runs 900 m, C runs 850 m. In 2700 m, C runs 2700 × 850/900 = 2550 m. B beats C by 150 m.

questions.title: Distance to the Place
questions.question: A man can row 6 km/hr in still water. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/hr, it takes him 3 hours to row to a place and back. How far (km) is the place?

questions.title: First Meeting on Circular Track
questions.question: Two persons start running simultaneously around a circular track of length 300 m from the same point at speeds 15 km/hr and 25 km/hr. When (in seconds) will they meet for the first time on the track, if they move in opposite directions?
questions.solution: Relative speed = 40 km/hr = 100/9 m/s. Time = 300 × 9/100 = 27 sec.

questions.title: 16 April 1976
questions.question: Find the day of the week of April 16th, 1976, if April 16th, 1974 was Tuesday.
questions.solution: From 16 April 1974 to 16 April 1976 = 365 + 366 = 731 days (1976 is a leap year and Feb 29 is included). 731 mod 7 = 3 odd days. Tuesday + 3 = Friday.

questions.title: 15 January 1979
questions.question: Find the day of the week on 15th January, 1979.
questions.solution: 1 January 1979 was a Monday (counting back 22 years from 1 Jan 2001, a Monday, gives 22 × 365 + 6 = 8036 days ≡ 0 mod 7). So 15 Jan 1979 is also a Monday.

questions.title: 23 December 2003
questions.question: If 23rd May, 2003 is a Friday, what day of the week will be 23rd December?
questions.solution: Days from 23 May to 23 Dec = 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 = 214. 214 mod 7 = 4. Friday + 4 = Tuesday.

questions.title: 3 January 1993
questions.question: January 3rd, 1992 was a Friday. What day of the week was January 3rd, 1993?
questions.solution: 1992 is a leap year, so 366 days = 2 odd days. Friday + 2 = Sunday.

questions.title: 28 May 2003
questions.question: On which day of the week does 28th May, 2003 fall?
questions.solution: 23 May 2003 is Friday (reference), so 28 May = Friday + 5 = Wednesday.

questions.title: 28 May 1991
questions.question: If your birthday is on 28th May, 1991, then what day was it?
questions.solution: From 28 May 1991 to 28 May 2003 = 12 years with 3 leap days (1992, 1996, 2000) = 15 odd days = 1. 28 May 2003 is a Wednesday, so 28 May 1991 was a Tuesday.

questions.title: 1 March 1990
questions.question: What day of the week is 1st March, 1990?
questions.solution: 1 Jan 1990 was a Monday. 1 March is 31 + 28 = 59 days later, 59 mod 7 = 3, so Monday + 3 = Thursday.

questions.title: Same Calendar as 2007
questions.question: Which year will have the same calendar as that of 2007?
questions.solution: 2007 is a non-leap year starting on Monday. The next non-leap year starting on Monday is 2018.

questions.title: Same Calendar as 2001
questions.question: Which year will have the same calendar as that of 2001?
questions.solution: 2001 is a non-leap year starting on Monday. The next non-leap year starting on Monday is 2007.

questions.title: 4 June 2001
questions.question: You entered the college for the first time on 4th June, 2001. What was the day?
questions.solution: 1 Jan 2001 was a Monday. 4 June is the 155th day, so 154 days later. 154 mod 7 = 0, so it is a Monday.

questions.title: Hands Pointing Opposite
questions.question: How many times do the hands of a clock point towards each other (opposite directions) in a day?
questions.solution: The hands are opposite 11 times in 12 hours, so 22 times in a day.

questions.title: Clock Gaining 5 Minutes
questions.question: A clock which gains 5 minutes in every two hours is set at 12.00 P.M. on a certain day. Find the time shown by the watch on the next day at 11 A.M.
questions.solution: Real time elapsed = 23 hours. Gain = 23 × 5/2 = 57.5 min. Watch shows 11:00 AM + 57.5 min = 11:57:30 AM.

questions.title: Clock Losing 10 Seconds
questions.question: A clock which loses 10 seconds in every minute is set at 2.00 P.M. on a certain day. Find the time shown by the watch on the next day at 8 P.M.
questions.solution: Real time elapsed = 30 hours. The watch runs at 50/60 = 5/6 speed, so it shows 25 hours elapsed. 2 PM + 25 h = 3 PM next day.

questions.title: Clock Losing 50 Seconds
questions.question: A clock which loses 50 seconds every two minutes is set at 6.00 P.M. on a certain day. What is the time shown by this watch on the next day if the current time is 3.00 P.M?
questions.solution: Real time elapsed = 21 hours. The watch runs at 70/120 = 7/12 speed, so it shows 21 × 7/12 = 12.25 h. 6 PM + 12 h 15 min = 6:15 AM.

questions.title: Hands Coincide
questions.question: How many times do the hands of a clock coincide in a day?
questions.solution: The hands coincide 11 times in 12 hours, so 22 times in a day.

questions.title: Hands at Right Angles
questions.question: How many times are the hands of a clock at right angles in a day?
questions.solution: They are at right angles 22 times in 12 hours, so 44 times in a day.

questions.title: Angle at 2:45
questions.question: What is the angle (in degrees) between the hands of the clock at 2:45?
questions.solution: Hour hand = 2 × 30 + 45 × 0.5 = 82.5°. Minute hand = 45 × 6 = 270°. Difference = 187.5°, so the smaller angle = 360 − 187.5 = 172.5°.

questions.title: Angle at 9 O'clock
questions.question: At 9 O'clock find the angle (in degrees) between the hands of the clock.
questions.solution: At 9 the hour hand is at 270° and the minute hand at 0°, so the angle = 90°.

questions.title: Hands Coincide Between 6 and 7
questions.question: At what time between 6 O'clock and 7 O'clock will the hands of the clock coincide?
questions.solution: Minute hand gains 5.5° per minute. Needed gain = 180°, so t = 180/5.5 = 360/11 = 32 8/11 min past 6.

questions.title: Right Angle Between 3 and 4
questions.question: At what time between 3 O'clock and 4 O'clock will the hands of the clock be at right angles?
questions.solution: At 3:00 the hands are already 90° apart. The minute hand must gain 180° over the hour hand: t = 180/5.5 = 32 8/11 min past 3.

questions.title: Subtract to Make Divisible by 9
questions.question: What is the smallest number that when subtracted from 63407 makes it exactly divisible by 9?
questions.solution: Digit sum = 6+3+4+0+7 = 20, and 20 mod 9 = 2. Subtract 2.

questions.title: Remainder of 3^51 by 5
questions.question: Find the remainder when 3^51 is divided by 5.

questions.title: Divisibility by 90
questions.question: If the number 653ab is divisible by 90, then (a + b) = ?
questions.solution: Divisible by 10 → b = 0. Divisible by 9 → 6+5+3+a+0 = 14 + a is a multiple of 9 → a = 4. a + b = 4.

questions.title: Unit Digit of Sum
questions.question: What would be the unit digit in the answer of: 369^28 + 167^44?
questions.solution: Unit digit of 9^28 = 1 (even power). Unit digit of 7^44 = 1 (44 is a multiple of 4). Sum's unit digit = 1 + 1 = 2.

questions.title: Least Number Leaving Remainder 3
questions.question: What is the least number that when divided by any of the numbers 7, 16, 28 leaves a remainder of 3?

questions.title: Neither Prime nor Composite
questions.question: The only natural number which is neither prime nor composite is?
questions.solution: 1 has only one divisor, so it is neither prime nor composite.

questions.title: Largest 5-digit Multiple of 99
questions.question: Which is the largest number of 5 digits that is divisible by 99?
questions.solution: 99999 / 99 = 1010 remainder 9. Largest multiple = 99999 − 9 = 99990.

questions.title: Greatest Length of Scale
questions.question: What should be the greatest possible length (in cm) of a scale which can be used to measure exactly the lengths 7 m, 3 m 85 cm and 12 m 95 cm?
questions.solution: Lengths in cm: 700, 385, 1295. HCF = 35 cm.

questions.title: Least Multiple of 7 with Remainder 4
questions.question: Find the least multiple of 7 which leaves a remainder of 4 when divided by 6, 9, 15 and 18.
questions.solution: LCM(6, 9, 15, 18) = 90, so the number is 90k + 4. We need 90k + 4 ≡ 0 (mod 7) → 6k + 4 ≡ 0 → k ≡ 4. Number = 364 = 7 × 52.
